subject: RFI: Audit log serialization, retention SLAs, and exportability
messages:
From: Audra Mills <audra.mills@pioneerfin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Audit log serialization, retention SLAs, and exportability

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking the time on the call earlier. As part of our procurement RFI we need concrete answers to Pioneer Financial's logging and audit trail requirements. Could you please confirm the following items so we can include them in our security review? Prefer short, definitive answers and any accompanying artifacts (schema, sample exports).

1) Supported export serialization formats (preferred: NDJSON/Parquet/Avro). Are exports compressed/streamable for large windows?
2) Schema versioning strategy — how are breaking changes communicated? Do you publish a stable audit schema?
3) Retention enforcement — what controls exist for minimum/maximum retention per account and how are legal hold/deletion requests handled?
4) Delivery SLAs for ad-hoc exports (e.g., 90th percentile within X hours for 30 days of logs) and tooling for incremental slices (time-range, user-id, session-id).
5) Tamper-evidence: do exported archives include signed manifests, checksums, or timestamped digests?
6) Redaction/PII: support for field-level redaction in exports and opt-in pseudonymization for sensitive fields.
7) Live-forwarding: can logs be streamed to S3/GCS/SFTP in near-real time and what guarantees exist for ordering?

We'd like a response by EOD PT tomorrow (18 May) to keep the procurement timeline. If you have a sample export that demonstrates schema and checksum metadata, please attach.

Best,
Audra
Security Architect, Pioneer Financial

---
Pioneer Financial procurement: procurement@pioneerfin.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Audra Mills <audra.mills@pioneerfin.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Audit log serialization, retention SLAs, and exportability

Audra — thanks for the clear list. We're putting together a concise RFI response and will include artifacts. High-level answers below; I'll attach a small sample export + schema and our SOC2 summary. If you want, we can follow up with a short walkthrough.

1) Formats & compression: Exports available as NDJSON and Parquet. We produce streamable NDJSON.gz (chunked) for large windows and Parquet for columnar analytics. Avro is available on request.

2) Schema versioning: We publish an audit-schema with semantic versioning (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Breaking changes are announced 60 days prior with migration notes; we maintain a backward-compatibility shim for one major version when feasible. Schema file attached (audit_schema_v2.json).

3) Retention enforcement: Retention is configurable per-tenant. Hosted customers can select retention windows from 30 days up to 7 years (policy tiers). For Dedicated/Private deployments we support policy lockdowns controlled by the customer's admin. Deletion requests: immediate logical deletion of active indices plus a controlled physical purge process (documented runbook). Legal holds override retention and prevent deletion until released.

4) Export SLAs: Standard ad-hoc export SLA is 95th percentile within 8 business hours for up to 30 days of logs (NDJSON.gz). For larger windows or expedited delivery we offer an accelerated export option (expedite queue) with 4-hour SLA for customers on Dedicated or enterprise plans. Exports support slicing by time-range, user_id, session_id, request_id, and custom tags.

5) Tamper-evidence: Exports include a signed manifest containing SHA-256 checksums for each chunk and a timestamped signature using our signing key. We also include a per-export manifest.json with a redwood_export_version and signatures. For higher-assurance flows we can provide a signed timestamp from our KMS/HSM gateway and a detachable SGN file. Sample export attached (sample_export_20270517.ndjson.gz) — manifest included.

6) Redaction & pseudonymization: Two options — pre-export field-level redaction (configurable allowlist/denylist) and deterministic pseudonymization for identifiers (HMAC-based tokenization) with customer-provided salt. Live fields that are redacted are annotated in the manifest.

7) Live-forwarding: Near-real-time delivery to S3/GCS/SFTP via our forwarder. Ordering guarantees: per-shard append ordering with at-least-once delivery semantics; we include sequence numbers and per-shard checkpoints to reconcile duplicates. For strict ordering we recommend the dedicated forwarder sink (included with Dedicated or Private).

Attachments: audit_schema_v2.json, sample_export_20270517.ndjson.gz, redwood_soc2_report_2026.pdf

I'll send a compact RFI doc with the bullets above and the sample export within the hour. If you need a signed attestation or a checksum validation walkthrough, loop in your infra/security ops and we can set up a 30-min session.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Head of Compliance & Product Security, Redwood Inference

From: Audra Mills <audra.mills@pioneerfin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Audit log serialization, retention SLAs, and exportability

Soojin — thanks, that is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we finalize the RFP section:

• Schema drift: can you provide an example of a non-breaking vs breaking change and what the migration note looks like?
• Signed manifests: do you provide the public verification key or support verification via a published key endpoint?
• Legal hold workflow: outline the steps Pioneer would take and expected timelines for release after hold expiration.

Also: do you have a small NDJSON sample we can run through our ingestion pipeline (just 100–200 lines)? The manifest + checksum will help us validate integrity checks automatically.

If you can attach the sample NDJSON (non-archived) and a short legal-hold playbook, we can proceed.

Regards,
Audra

Subject: Re: RFI: Audit log serialization, retention SLAs, and exportability

Audra — attaching the non-archived NDJSON sample and a short legal-hold playbook as requested. Quick answers inline and artifacts attached.

• Schema drift example: Non-breaking: adding an optional field "geo.country" (minor bump). Breaking: renaming event_type -> activity_type (major bump) — migration note includes example rewrites and a deprecation window. We include sample migration snippets in the schema repo.

• Public key verification: We publish a rotating verification endpoint (https://keys.redwood.com/exports/v1) and provide a per-export x509 signature bundle. Verification steps are in the README attached.

• Legal hold workflow (summary): 1) Pioneer Security sends legal-hold request to legal-holds@redwood.com with hold-id and scope; 2) Redwood acknowledges within 2 hours and applies hold within 4 hours (logical hold flag); 3) Hold release requires signed approval from Pioneer legal and Redwood counsel; 4) Upon release, physical purge scheduled per policy (default 30 days) unless expedited. We'll include playbook PDF in Drive link.

Attachments: sample_audit_100lines.ndjson (100 lines, non-archived), legal_hold_playbook.pdf, audit_schema_v2.json (again), sample_export_20270517_manifest.json

Next steps: I'll drop the manifest verification steps and a short validation script in the Drive folder and invite your infra team. If you'd like, Laura can run a live checksum verification session with your SREs.

Thanks — talk soon.

Soojin
Head of Compliance & Product Security, Redwood Inference
